onTime.title: Delivered when I said
onTime.body: If I say Thursday, it is Thursday. No invoice for "unexpected complexity" — I quote what I can actually deliver.

real.title: Real, not a demo
real.body: Something your team uses on a normal Tuesday. Deployed, documented, and handed over with everything it needs to keep running.

custom.title: Built for your problem
custom.body: Your workflow is not a template, so the solution isn't either. I start from what your business actually does, not from a tutorial.

support.title: I don't disappear
support.body: Handoff isn't the end of the conversation. You get support after delivery, and a person who still answers their email.

services.title: Start with a conversation.
services.intro: Most AI projects go wrong before a line of code is written — the wrong problem gets picked. So we start by finding the right one.

consultation.name: AI Strategy Consultation
consultation.summary: One focused call about your business and where AI genuinely fits — and, just as often, where it doesn't. Bring a problem, not a technology.
consultation.p1: A clear read on which of your problems AI can actually solve today, and which are better solved another way.
consultation.p2: A realistic scope: what it would take to build, roughly how long, and what could go wrong.
consultation.p3: A written summary after the call, so you can share it with your team without relying on your notes.
consultation.note: Online booking and payment are opening soon.

webinars.name: Webinars
webinars.summary: Live sessions on putting AI to work in a real business — practical, in plain language, with the code shown on screen.

classes.name: Online classes
classes.summary: Structured courses for teams who want to build their own AI capability instead of outsourcing it forever.

projects.title: A portfolio you can run.
projects.intro: My rule: build everything in public. Every project here is deployed, open source and documented — something you can open and try, not a claim you have to trust.
projects.emptyState: The first projects are being built right now, in public. Each one lands here only once it is deployed, open source and documented — never before.

about.title: Hi, I'm Roya.
about.p1: I'm an AI engineer and software developer based in Turin, Italy. I build applications powered by large language models — RAG tools, assistants and agents that do a specific job for a specific business.
about.p2: I came to this work later than some, and that turned out to be the useful part: I've been the person on the other side of a software project, waiting for an update that never came. I build the way I wished someone had built for me.

aboutPage.metaDescription: Roya Vosoughi — AI engineer and software developer in Turin, Italy. Building AI-powered applications in public.
aboutPage.title: I build the way I wished someone had built for me.
aboutPage.lead: AI engineer and software developer in Turin, Italy. I make large language models do specific, useful jobs for real businesses.
aboutPage.p1: My work is mostly applications powered by LLMs: retrieval systems that answer questions from a company's own documents, assistants that handle a repetitive task properly, and agents that know the limits of what they should decide alone.
aboutPage.p2: I have one rule that shapes everything: build in public. Every project is deployed, open source and documented. That is partly discipline — it is much harder to cut a corner when the repository is open — and partly the fastest way to show what I can do without asking anyone to take my word for it.
aboutPage.p3: I studied computer engineering at Politecnico di Torino. I work in English with clients across Italy and Europe, and in Persian with Persian-speaking businesses.

punctual.name: Punctuality
punctual.body: The project arrives when I said it would. Your time is the one thing I cannot give back to you.

practical.name: Practicality
practical.body: A solution that works in the business, not a demo that works in a meeting.

creative.name: Creativity
creative.body: A specific answer to your specific problem, rather than last project's answer with the name changed.

inspiring.name: Possibility
inspiring.body: I want you to leave knowing what AI could do for you — including, honestly, when the answer is not much.

aboutPage.ctaBody: Tell me what the problem is. If I'm not the right person for it, I'll say so and point you somewhere better.
